# Panko

> Panko is a high-performance JSON serializer for ActiveRecord and Ruby objects. It compiles a specialized serializer, in pure Ruby, once per serializer class (there is no native extension), builds JSON incrementally with Oj::StringWriter, and resolves serializer metadata ahead of time — so per-record serialization is straight-line code with minimal allocations.

The public API is small and stable: subclass `Panko::Serializer` and declare `attributes`, `has_one` / `has_many`, and method attributes; serialize a single object with `#serialize` (returns a Hash) or `#serialize_to_json` (returns a JSON String), and a collection with `Panko::ArraySerializer`.

## Docs

- [Introduction](https://panko.dev/): What Panko is and the three choices behind its speed.
- [Getting Started](https://panko.dev/getting-started): Install Panko and write your first serializer, including collection and Rails-controller usage.
- [Performance](https://panko.dev/performance): Benchmark methodology plus Panko's throughput and allocation numbers across serializer shapes.
- [Design Choices](https://panko.dev/design-choices): How Panko is fast — code generation, incremental JSON with Oj::StringWriter, and ahead-of-time metadata.

## Reference

- [Serializers](https://panko.dev/serializers): The `Panko::Serializer` / `Panko::ArraySerializer` API — serialize methods, constructor options (`context`, `scope`, `only`, `except`), and `SKIP`.
- [Attributes](https://panko.dev/attributes): Field attributes, method attributes (with `object` / `context` / `scope`), and `aliases`.
- [Associations](https://panko.dev/associations): `has_one` and `has_many`, output-key aliasing, and serializer inference.
- [Filters](https://panko.dev/filters): `only` / `except`, nested filters, and `filters_for`.
- [Response](https://panko.dev/response-bag): `Panko::Response` and `Panko::JsonValue` for composing serialized output into a larger JSON response.

## Optional

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/yosiat/panko_serializer): Source, issues, and changelog.
